verdict: OK to lend in Noida electronic components and PCBs, but only to B2B PCB/PCBA makers with pass-through pricing and tight inventory discipline; avoid consumer-durable-linked assemblers and thin-networth capex-heavy units.
title: Noida electronic components & PCBs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A PCB or component unit buys copper-clad laminate, gold, solder and chemicals, runs plating, etching and drilling lines, and sells boards or assemblies to OEMs on a one-quarter price-pass-through lag [7].** Cash sits in inventory and receivables, not in the machine: a peer's working capital intensity was 45% in FY2021 on high inventory and receivable days [11]. So when a proposal lands, check inventory days and receivable days first; if inventory is held to meet minimum order quantities [11], ask what share is customer-committed versus speculative.

## What has changed now
**Input costs are moving against the maker: copper-clad laminate rose 13% and gold also rose, squeezing PCB input costs, with recovery only from Q4FY26 [7].** Consumer-durable-linked PCBA demand is soft [7], and RAC demand swung from Q1 down ~5-10% to Q2 down ~35% [4]. India-wide IIP for NIC 26 is +19.3% YoY and +13.6% Apr-to-date [D], and exports are +44.0% Apr-to-date in USD [D] — so the export-facing B2B book is running ahead of the domestic consumer book. UP GST collections are +14.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D].

## Where the growth is in Noida
**UP contributes about 55% of India's mobile phone production and 60% of its electronic component manufacturing [1], and the state is courting a 500-acre 'Singapore City' in YEIDA Sector 7 for semiconductor fabrication, logistics and data centres [1][2].** HCL has submitted an SEZ proposal for a semiconductor hub in Greater Noida [3]. These are proposals, not orders — collect from customer any confirmed offtake before you size a facility. Pursue B2B PCB/PCBA suppliers to mobile and telecom OEMs, and component makers with multi-vertical order books beyond consumer durables [7]. Avoid assemblers whose sole end-market is room air conditioners [4] and thin-networth units funding capex on debt — a peer carried networth of Rs.16.40 crore with TOL/TNW at 1.97 times and gearing expected to rise on debt-funded capex [10].

## How to grow safely
**Structure term debt to the capex only, keep working capital as a separate cash-credit line sized to the 45% intensity peer benchmark [11], and take a quarterly price-pass-through covenant because the lag is one quarter [7].** Take monthly stock statements and ageing; take GST returns monthly to confirm the +14.2% UP trend [D] is showing in the borrower's own filings. For any SEZ or Singapore City-linked proposal [1][2][3], ask for the lease or allotment letter and the customer's purchase order — collect from customer.

## Early warning signs
**Watch for receivable days stretching past the one-quarter pass-through window [7], inventory build without matching orders [11], and any shift of sales mix toward consumer durables [7].** A rating report on a PCB peer is dated March 2024 [10] and the peer result notes carry no clear date [4][5][7] — treat them as directional, not current. Local sources say little about Noida's own component units; the Singapore City and HCL items are announcements [1][2][3], so lean on first principles and the peer numbers above.
watch: Receivable days exceed one quarter -> ask for customer payment confirmation and reprice the limit
Filing turnover falls below the UP +14.2% trend [D] -> freeze fresh disbursement and review
Copper-clad laminate or gold cost rise not passed within one quarter [7] -> cut limit or demand margin support
Consumer-durable share of sales rises [7] -> treat as concentration and cap exposure
No lease or purchase order on file for SEZ/Singapore City-linked capex [1][2][3] -> hold term loan
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
